text:
Step 1: Import

raw <- read_sheet("https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1e8XSidxeT3SIE10g1jiEuALRa7REpmYU64_3V3TNKKs/edit?usp=sharing") %>%
  rename(
    timestamp       = Timestamp,
    zipcode         = `What is the zipcode of your hometown?`,
    stats_before    = `Have you taken any statistics courses before?`,
    prog_experience = `How much experience do you have with programming?`,
    languages       = `If you've programmed before, which languages have you used, and how comfortable do you feel with each? If you haven't programmed before, please leave this question blank.`,
    data_interest   = `What types of data interest you?`,
    learn_best      = `How do you learn best?`,
    commute_min     = `How long does it take you to commute from home to this classroom, in minutes? Please enter a number only.`
  )

title: AE04 - Getting to Know Your Data Types
text:
Step 2: Data type audit

“How long does it take you to commute from home to this classroom, in minutes? Please enter a number only.”

class(raw$commute_min)

[1] "list"


Is that what you’d expect, given the question?
No. I would expect an integer/number.

mean(raw$commute_min)

[1] NA


What’s going on? unlist() this variable and look at the unique() values.

unlist(raw$commute_min)

 [1] "10"      "7"       "10"      "10"      "15"      "21"      "35"     
 [8] "25"      "15"      "30"      "15"      "70"      "15"      "20"     
[15] "10"      "70"      "10"      "20"      "15"      "15"      "35"     
[22] "16"      "10"      "22"      "forever" "15"      "30"      "30"     
[29] "35"     




“How much experience do you have with programming?”

class(raw$prog_experience)

[1] "character"

table(raw$prog_experience)


A lot — I use programming regularly and feel confident writing code 
                                                                 11 
                                                               None 
                                                                  1 
       Some — I’ve worked on a few projects or used it occasionally 
                                                                 18 


Is this variable ordinal? Does everything you’d expect to see actually show up?


Skim the rest

glimpse(raw)

Rows: 30
Columns: 8
$ timestamp       <dttm> 2026-08-24 15:32:06, 2026-08-24 15:32:19, 2026-08-24 …
$ zipcode         <dbl> 95618, 95129, 95932, 94526, 95973, 94550, 96080, 94510…
$ stats_before    <chr> "Yes, I have taken another college course on statistic…
$ prog_experience <chr> "A lot — I use programming regularly and feel confiden…
$ languages       <chr> "C/C++ (very comfortable), Python (somewhat comfortabl…
$ data_interest   <chr> "- Crime, - Economics, - Environment/Climate, - Politi…
$ learn_best      <chr> "Engaging lectures", "In person classes and lectures",…
$ commute_min     <list> 10, 7, 10, 10, 15, 21, 35, 25, 15, <NULL>, 30, 15, 70…


For each of the other variables — is R’s type what you’d expect, given the question that was asked? We won’t work with them further in this AE, but you should still be able to answer this for each one.

title: AE04 - Getting to Know Your Data Types
text:
Step 3: Apply fixes

Commute time
While we could try to coerce list → character → numeric, it’s easier here to specify data types on read.

raw <- read_sheet("https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1e8XSidxeT3SIE10g1jiEuALRa7REpmYU64_3V3TNKKs/edit?usp=sharing", col_types = c("Dccccccn")) %>%
  rename(
    timestamp       = Timestamp,
    zipcode         = `What is the zipcode of your hometown?`,
    stats_before    = `Have you taken any statistics courses before?`,
    prog_experience = `How much experience do you have with programming?`,
    languages       = `If you've programmed before, which languages have you used, and how comfortable do you feel with each? If you haven't programmed before, please leave this question blank.`,
    data_interest   = `What types of data interest you?`,
    learn_best      = `How do you learn best?`,
    commute_min     = `How long does it take you to commute from home to this classroom, in minutes? Please enter a number only.`
  )

Always keep an eye out for this, and ask yourself whether it’s expected, given what you found in Step 2.

class(raw$commute_min)

[1] "numeric"




Recode & reorder prog_experience

First, confirm what’s actually in the data.


table(raw$prog_experience)


A lot — I use programming regularly and feel confident writing code 
                                                                 11 
                                                               None 
                                                                  1 
       Some — I’ve worked on a few projects or used it occasionally 
                                                                 18 

glimpse(raw$prog_experience)

 chr [1:30] "A lot — I use programming regularly and feel confident writing code" ...

typeof(raw$prog_experience)

[1] "character"



Then compare against the published survey. Is everything you’d expect to see actually there?


No. I’m missing the category “A little…”


Convert the variable to a factor with the current recorded levels.


raw$prog_experience <- factor(raw$prog_experience, levels = c("None", "Some — I’ve worked on a few projects or used it occasionally", "A lot — I use programming regularly and feel confident writing code"))


Now that it’s reading as a factor, use fct_expand() to add any level that’s missing.


fct_expand(raw$prog_experience, "A little — I’ve written a few lines or done small exercises")

Last, respect the ordinal nature of this variable by putting the levels in increasing order.
